advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Check the returncode/empty stdout of `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` in `_committed_project_layer` and raise ConfigError on failure (also catch ValueError from `relative_to`).
evidence: src/rebar/_opcert_gate_config.py:121: top = _git(root, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel").stdout.strip()
src/rebar/_opcert_gate_config.py:122: rel = PurePosixPath(Path(root).resolve().relative_to(Path(top).resolve()).as_posix())
Every other `_git` call in the module checks returncode (lines 79, 84, 102, 107); this one does not.
src/rebar/_commands/verify_opcert.py:119 only catches `config.ConfigError`, so a ValueError from relative_to escapes the documented exit-2 path.
advisory.finding: `_committed_project_layer` never checks the exit status of `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`. If the call fails, `top` is "", and `Path("").resolve()` is the process cwd. `relative_to` then either raises an uncaught ValueError (a traceback instead of the documented exit 2) or walks paths computed against the wrong base, all inside the gate's trust-config resolution.
scenarios: `git remote` succeeds but `--show-toplevel` fails, e.g. a bare repo or GIT_DIR set without a work tree, or a root reached through a path git refuses: the gate crashes, or resolves the project layer against cwd instead of the repo.
advisory.suggested_fix: top_proc = _git(root, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"); if top_proc.returncode != 0 or not top_proc.stdout.strip(): raise ConfigError(f"op-cert gate: git rev-parse --show-toplevel failed in {root}: {top_proc.stderr.strip()}"); then wrap relative_to in try/except ValueError -> ConfigError.

The repo's only CI consumer had to be changed to keep working: .github/workflows/verify-identity.yml:142 adds `git fetch ... '+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main'` before `rebar verify-opcert`. Any other pipeline invoking the documented CLI (docs/cli-reference.md:897, infra/runbooks/mcp-opcert-enforcement-flip.md:63,118) without that fetch now exits 2.

docs/api-stability.md:22-23: CLI behaviour changes are expected to be communicated. No release-notes or CHANGELOG entry is part of this change; the diff touches only cli-reference, exit-codes, manifest-signing, plan-review-gate and the runbook.
advisory.finding: The op-cert gate hard-codes `refs/remotes/origin/main` as the reviewed base and gives no way to override it. Any checkout that has a remote but no `origin/main` used to run `rebar verify-opcert` normally and now fails with exit 2. That covers a remote not named `origin`, a default branch other than `main`, and a CI checkout that fetches only the change ref. The sibling attested gates resolve the same base through `REBAR_GATE_REF` and `[snapshot].ref`, which this gate ignores. Previously valid input is now rejected, with no migration path other than fetching or creating a ref named `origin/main`.
scenarios: A downstream project whose default branch is `master` or `trunk` runs `rebar verify-opcert` in CI and now always gets exit 2.
A fork whose base remote is named `upstream` gets exit 2 even after fetching its base.
A CI job such as the default actions/checkout fetches only the PR ref and gets exit 2 until a main fetch step is added.
advisory.suggested_fix: In `base_ref`, use `REBAR_GATE_REF` (or a value from the trusted env/user/cli layers) when it is set, and otherwise fall back to `refs/remotes/origin/main`. Do not read `[snapshot].ref` from the working-tree project config, so the change still cannot pick its own base. Add a docs/release-notes.md entry describing the new exit-2 condition and the fetch it requires.

advisory.finding: In the GitHub Actions lane, the 'main-only config' protection is enforced by code the change under test supplies. The workflow runs `pip install -e .` on the PR checkout and runs on `pull_request` with the PR's own copy of verify-identity.yml. A change can edit src/rebar/_opcert_gate_config.py (for example, make gate_config return compose_config(root)), or edit the verify-opcert step itself, and so widen its own gate run. Meanwhile, the CLI help, cli-reference.md, manifest-signing.md and plan-review-gate.md now state without qualification that 'a change cannot widen its own gate'.
scenarios: A PR changes rebar.toml to add its own key to trusted_opcert_keys and also patches _opcert_gate_config.base_ref to return None. The PR's verify-identity run installs that patched code, falls back to the working tree, trusts the PR's key, and passes.
A PR deletes the `git fetch` line or replaces `rebar verify-opcert` with `true` in verify-identity.yml. The pull_request run uses the modified workflow.
advisory.suggested_fix: In the verify-opcert step, install rebar from origin/main (for example, `git worktree add /tmp/gate origin/main && pip install /tmp/gate`), or run this gate from a workflow the PR cannot modify (pull_request_target with no PR code execution, or the Gerrit verifier). Alternatively, add a qualifier to the doc statements saying the guarantee covers config only and needs a trusted gate binary.

Commit message claims "any CI provider, or none, gets the same rule", but a provider whose checkout has no remote gets the working-tree rule.
src/rebar/_commands/verify_opcert.py:122 only prints the trust source to stderr; there is no other signal that the base-branch check never ran.
dropped.finding: The working-tree fallback triggers whenever `git remote` prints nothing. Whether a checkout has a remote depends on how CI provisioned it, not on whether a change is under review. A CI that builds a remote-less checkout (git init + fetch by URL/sha, an exported tree, some Gerrit/Zuul-style job workspaces) silently gets the change's own rebar.toml. That brings back the self-widening this commit fixes, and the exit status does not change; only a stderr note shows it.
scenarios: A non-GitHub CI lane initialises a fresh repo and fetches the change by sha with no named remote: verify-opcert reads the change's rebar.toml, which can list its own key or drop require_environment, and passes.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Decode `git show` output as UTF-8 explicitly (e.g. `encoding="utf-8"`, or read bytes and call `tomllib.loads(stdout.decode("utf-8"))` with a ConfigError on decode failure).
evidence: src/rebar/_opcert_gate_config.py:61-67: subprocess.run([...], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT_S, check=False)
src/rebar/_opcert_gate_config.py:68: except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc: — a UnicodeDecodeError is not caught
src/rebar/_config_sources.py:128-129: with open(path, "rb") as f: data = tomllib.load(f)
rebar.toml:1 contains non-ASCII (`—`) in the committed project config
dropped.finding: The committed config blob is decoded with the locale's text encoding (`text=True` with no `encoding`). The working-tree reader opens the file in binary and lets tomllib decode it as UTF-8. Under a non-UTF-8 locale, the repo's non-ASCII rebar.toml can be mis-decoded, or raise UnicodeDecodeError, which `_git` does not catch. Main's config would then parse differently from the same file read from disk, or crash the gate.
scenarios: The gate runs on a host whose preferred encoding is not UTF-8 (e.g. Windows cp1252, or a POSIX locale without UTF-8 coercion).
dropped.suggested_fix: In `_git`, pass `encoding="utf-8", errors="strict"` in place of relying on `text=True`, and add UnicodeDecodeError to the caught exceptions, mapped to ConfigError.
